## [#10938: fix(Toolbar): keep focus on the clicked button](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/pull/10938)

- **Change:** high complexity by step 1's core-behavior rule, despite only five changed source lines and eight added test lines: Toolbar's shared hook stops restoring the previous button when focus returns via a pointer interaction. RAC Toolbar users retain keyboard restoration, with an added rendered-focus regression sequence; the medium/high review is limited to summary, API/compatibility, duplicates and readiness rather than the full low-complexity red-flag review.
- **Compatibility / reviewer attention:** [useToolbar.ts lines 138-146](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/blob/9e2cdab2be9932af0e2db818eb0e307df5a05668/packages/react-aria/src/toolbar/useToolbar.ts#L138-L146) gates `lastFocused.current?.focus()` on `isFocusVisible()` and still clears the saved element. No public prop, export, type, event, default, DOM, class, data-attribute or CSS-variable change is present in the diff. This changes existing focus behavior for pointer-origin re-entry, including programmatic focus while pointer modality remains active, rather than detecting a click specifically: [main's helper at lines 320-322](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/blob/82959b6a9ac4ea717228636b99fc8fd24736a7f4/packages/react-aria/src/interactions/useFocusVisible.ts#L320-L322) returns `currentModality !== 'pointer'`, preserving virtual as well as keyboard restoration. Ask the reviewer to confirm that broader modality boundary is intended. No separate `needs API review` proposal for this corrective behavior change on current evidence.
- **Issue / verification:** [#10934](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/issues/10934) describes Tab out, click a different button, Tab out and Shift+Tab back, with the clicked button expected to retain focus; it reports Chrome, Firefox and Safari and contains no comments or maintainer direction to contradict. The added [Toolbar.test.tsx lines 303-310](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/blob/9e2cdab2be9932af0e2db818eb0e307df5a05668/packages/react-aria-components/test/Toolbar.test.tsx#L303-L310) asserts actual button focus after clicking and later keyboard re-entry, not private state. The issue supplies manual verification instructions, but no browser-specific result for the fix is provided. Main's existing test explicitly describes jsdom Tab limitations at [lines 253-257](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/blob/82959b6a9ac4ea717228636b99fc8fd24736a7f4/packages/react-aria-components/test/Toolbar.test.tsx#L253-L257); green CI does not establish cross-browser pointer behavior. Verification here was by reading only, not test execution or opening issue videos.
- **Duplicates / existing main:** searches covered #10934, Toolbar focus/click/last-focused behavior, `useToolbar` and recent `useToolbar.ts` mentions. No supported competing implementation was found. Closed [#5463](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/pull/5463) addresses native-element focus events, not clicked-button restoration; merged [#10712](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/pull/10712) changes arrow-key scrolling and explicitly leaves pointer focus alone. Neither is a duplicate of this fix. Main still unconditionally restores saved focus at [useToolbar.ts lines 134-142](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum/blob/82959b6a9ac4ea717228636b99fc8fd24736a7f4/packages/react-aria/src/toolbar/useToolbar.ts#L134-L142); the current Toolbar and useToolbar docs expose no dedicated restoration toggle. No equivalent documented solution or evidence that this was previously working was established, so no workaround or `regression` label is proposed.
